A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MINJA research and contain 35 pages, including Appendices A–O. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable matching of the main text, mathematics, tables, figures, and appendix material.

before.justification: v4 reports original experiments measuring injection success, attack success, and benign utility on MIMIC-III, eICU, Webshop, and MMLU, with additional ablations and repeated-run results in the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and the appendices, including attack evaluations, defense experiments, ablations, and stability measurements.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 and Appendix A retain the same bridging steps, indication prompts, and progressive shortening procedure. No algorithm component, objective, or agent procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same healthcare, shopping, and question-answering tasks using MIMIC-III, eICU, Webshop, and MMLU. The victim-target categories and additional test scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison variants are unchanged, including targeted/general detection in Table 5 and full, fewer-step, and absent PSS in Table 12. PANDORA remains a qualitative comparison in Table 6, not an added empirical baseline.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and the appendices retain the same models, query counts, victim-target pairs, memory initialization, retrieval settings, and ISR/ASR/UD metrics. Text crossing page boundaries does not change the reported protocols.

E4.justification: The retrieval, benign-density, prior-poisoning, defense, MMLU-utility, model-variant, and PSS analyses remain unchanged. Appendix E retains the same case studies, and no robustness or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains standard deviations across victim-target pairs. Appendix K and Table 11 retain the same three-run ASR stability evaluation, with no changes to run disclosure or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted findings, and qualitative examples are unchanged throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 1 retains overall ASRs of 57.0% for EHR(GPT-4) on MIMIC-III and 98.9% for RAP(GPT-4o) on Webshop.

T1.justification: The threat-model assumptions and mathematical definitions of memory records, attack objectives, and shortening steps are unchanged. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about query-only memory injection, MINJA's effectiveness, and agent-memory vulnerabilities. The added code-access sentence does not revise the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same mechanism explanations, shared-memory assumption, interpretation of MMLU utility loss, caveat about weak models, defense limitations, and proposed applicability extensions.

D1.justification: v5 adds a direct GitHub code-repository link in the abstract; v4 only promises a future code release. Implementation details remain unchanged. The checklist still says code will be released later, so the PDFs establish a new access pointer without verifying repository availability or contents.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including Section 2's distinction from AgentPoison and Appendix F's conceptual comparison with PANDORA.

P1.justification: The abstract gains a code-access sentence, and Appendix D replaces the exposed '[Shen: at the end of the appendix]' note with ordinary prose. The arXiv version/date stamp updates; section order and narrative otherwise remain intact.

P2.justification: The abstract addition causes limited text reflow and changed page breaks through page 7. Figures and tables retain their designs, captions, and content; there is no substantive visual reorganization.

improvement.justification: The new abstract link supplies a concrete code-access pointer where v4 only promised a future release, and Appendix D removes an internal author note. These provide modest usability and editorial gains while the scientific evidence remains unchanged. The benefit is limited by unverified repository contents and the retained checklist statement that code will be released later.
